text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- A senior customs official and a regional border police chief have been held on suspicion of smuggling. The two are the highest-ranking customs and border police officials arrested on contraband charges.

- Ukio Bank intends to boost its share capital to 82 million litas from 42 million litas this year and to issue a GDR on the Luxembourg bourse. An earlier 18 million litas share emission was acquired by Nomura, which bought 14 million litas and Swedfund, which bought four million litas.
- The hard currency reserves of the Bank of Lithuania increased 2.6 times over three years and were $727 million at the end of November.
- The annual audit of the 1996 financial activities of the Bank of Lithuania will be carried out by Arthur Anderson.
- The trial of the alleged criminal boss Henrikas Daktaras has been delayed due to the illness of his defence attorney.

- As new Foreign Minister Algirdas Saudargas prepares for his first official visit to Poland and Germany, a senior foreign ministry official said that Warsaw and Bonn were the "essential axis" of Lithuanian foreign policy, uniting the country with European and trans-Atlantic structures.
- The trial of the alleged January 1991 coup plotters is expected to continue today.
